links: One straight leg swings under the body each step and tips forward like an inverted pendulum, trading potential for kinetic energy <- The valgus knee tucks that stance leg beneath the centre of mass and the short bowl pelvis steadies it with little side-to-side sway, so walking undercuts a knuckle-walk though not every other mammal's walk <- Gravity (9.8 m s^-2, F6) fixes the load each stance leg must counter <- Root: F23 bowl pelvis, valgus knee and Laetoli heel strike

Taking weight-bearing off the forelimbs frees both hands to carry provisions, tools and infants instead <- The same bowl pelvis narrows the birth canal, so infants are born helpless and must be carried for years; carrying, sweat cooling and running on a recoiling arch, not cheap distance alone, are what the package pays for <- Root: F27 secondary altricial infants and obligatory cooperative breeding

skill.effect: Walking steadily restores the creature's energy and leaves both hands free to carry supplies, while sprinting strongly drains that same energy.

chains.weakness: The bowl pelvis is both hip joint and birth canal: a hip hit halves move speed and caps carried load at 5 kg until it heals, wide loads will not fit through gaps it must pass, and every birth costs the group a rest day - aim for the hips, or wait for a labour.
observe: A single-file trail of footprints with a deep heel strike and a pushed-off big toe
A bowl-shaped fossil pelvis barely wider than the ribcage
An adult hauling food, a tool and an infant too young to walk

journal.en: Two legs free the hands; the bill comes due at birth.

analogues.organism: Homo sapiens / Australopithecus afarensis — inverted-pendulum striding gait with valgus knee and obstetric pelvis (same lineage as Laetoli trackmaker)
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Bare skin with millions of eccrine glands
links: Furless skin turns the whole body surface into a wet radiator <- Evaporative cooling is driven by air dryness, not breathing, so heat loss no longer caps muscle work <- A biped can therefore stay active at noon when furred competitors must lie in shade <- Root: 1361 W m^-2 solar flux at 1 AU sets the relentless heat load the body must dump
Every minute of that cooling is paid in water <- After 45 minutes it needs about 1.5 L or takes a dehydration penalty <- Root: F24 eccrine density

skill.effect: The creature powers through intense labor under the blazing sun for a short while without tiring, and can maintain a running pace while following a scent trail.

chains.weakness: Every minute of that cooling is paid in water: after 45 minutes it needs about 1.5 L or takes a dehydration penalty, and salt loss makes it slower to heal.
observe: Wet footprints that dry to a ring of salt
It keeps working at noon while furred animals are flat in the shade
It never pants, even when its chest is heaving

journal.en: The only hunter that pays for its speed in drinking water.

plausibility.summary: Label 'outwork furred pursuers at noon' as hypothesis, not established fact (F24). Passive could be 'extended heat-work window' with clear water debt, not guaranteed superiority over all diurnal competitors.
fixes: Label 'outwork furred pursuers at noon' as hypothesis, not established fact (F24). Passive could be 'extended heat-work window' with clear water debt, not guaranteed superiority over all diurnal competitors.

analogues.organism: Human eccrine-dominated thermoregulation (Wheeler); partial analogue — horse sweating and tongue/lung evaporative cooling in other endurance mammals, but not whole-body furless eccrine radiator
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: A saddle joint at the thumb base swings the pad round to face every fingertip <- The opposition geometry trades brute force for finely metered fingertip torque at low joint stress, so a precise pinch spends less energy than a power grip <- Small hard energy-dense packets - nuts, shellfish, marrow, knappable stone - reward that fine control every single day <- Root: F25 rotatable saddle-joint thumb and precision grip

Bipedalism took load-bearing off the forelimb, leaving the hand free to make precision a daily habit <- Chimpanzees and capuchins pinch too; what is new here is the degree of control and how often it is used, not the trick itself <- Root: F23 forelimbs freed by the striding bipedal package

skill.effect: In one action, open a seed, shellfish or knapped flake for food or a tool no other creature on the tile can use; the brute-force crush alternative takes two actions but breaks thick shells and jammed locks that the pinch cannot.

chains.weakness: Precision is bought with crush force: a thick shell or a locked joint defeats the pinch, and a grip on the wrist or a pinned thumb disables the hand entirely.
observe: A thumb pad worn flat and shiny at the tip
A stone struck at one consistent angle, leaving a row of identical flakes
A midden of cracked nutshells too small for any jaw on the tile

journal.en: It can pick a lock and cannot open a jar.

analogues.organism: Homo sapiens hand — trapeziometacarpal saddle joint and precision grip (Napier); convergent fine manipulation in capuchins (Cebus) and chimpanzees at lower duty cycle
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Held flame gelatinises starch and denatures protein outside the body, so tubers and tough meat pay more net calories per bite <- The measured gain is food- and method-specific: starch and collagen gain the most, fat can lose <- Combustion spreads only above roughly 16% O2, so the same air the creature breathes decides where cooking is even possible <- Root: F14 atmosphere at 21% O2 and F28 habitual fire

A ringed hearth is external digestion and a night guard post that predators learn to keep clear of <- Any shorter-gut-for-bigger-brain trade it permits is the debated expensive-tissue hypothesis, speculative and not settled <- Root: F28 habitual cooking from at least ~400 ka

skill.effect: A steady campfire keeps nearby predators at bay and thoroughly cooks gathered food, while its smoke drifts downwind in a visible, scented plume that can hide the camp's presence or send signals to allies.

chains.weakness: The flame dies without dry fuel or below about 16% O2, so rain, a soaked woodpile or thin air ends cooking and night defence, and anything downwind can follow the smoke cone straight to the camp.
observe: Charred bone and heat-cracked stone in a ring of cobbles
Starch grains split open in a way only heat produces
A camp that sleeps on the ground instead of in a tree

journal.en: It brought a small sun indoors, then complained about the smoke.

plausibility.summary: State +40% as upper-bound, food-specific (starch/collagen gain most; fat often little) per Carmody & Wrangham. Keep expensive-tissue brain–gut trade explicitly 'speculative' in skill text.
fixes: State +40% as upper-bound, food-specific (starch/collagen gain most; fat often little) per Carmody & Wrangham. Keep expensive-tissue brain–gut trade explicitly 'speculative' in skill text.

analogues.organism: Homo habituality with fire (~400 ka+); metabolic effect of cooking — gelatinisation/denaturation (Wrangham group); no non-human analogue for controlled hearth cooking
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: A steady, controlled exhale stacks into formant patterns - F1 and F2 fall as the vocal tract lengthens - so one breath can carry a three-step plan, not just an alarm <- FOXP2 tunes basal-ganglia sequencing of tongue, lips and breath, one contributor among many loci alongside orofacial motor control and social learning <- A descended larynx is not the trick itself: red deer and koalas lower theirs and never speak <- Root: F26 breath control, vocal learning and FOXP2 as one contributor

Scattered allies beyond sightlines and after dark still need shared plans, and gesture and gaze - the ape fallback - cannot cross 150 m or a ridge <- A shout carries roughly 150 m in open air, a number set by how 343 m s^-1 sound fades with distance, not by why the voice evolved <- Root: F11 sound speed in air sets the honest range

skill.effect: The creature clearly communicates a strategy to distant allies across open ground, and can whisper a secure version that remains hidden from enemies despite covering a shorter distance.

chains.weakness: Every shout is loud and honest: enemies in earshot hear the plan too and can ambush whoever answers, and the murmur variant covers only ~75 m, so a patient scout can slip inside it.
observe: A long call delivered on one steady, controlled exhale
Turn-taking: one voice answering another in rhythm, without overlap

journal.en: They rehearse tomorrow at the fire, and the wind sells every word.

plausibility.summary: Give plan-sharing range as ~50–150 m open air (terrain, humidity, voice effort); cite inverse-square + ground effect rather than fixing 150 m. Note murmur ~75 m is order-of-magnitude OK.

relations.note: Both track the same open-habitat pressure. Cenozoic cooling expanded grasslands, selecting for endurance over burst speed. Humans trade agility for striding and sweating; pronghorn trade maneuverability for massive cardio and panoramic vision. Playable: players can use human heat-dissipation to outlast pronghorn in summer, or follow pronghorn migration routes to find water.

Both solved fission-fusion sociality with vocal learning. Humans use speech and names; dolphins use signature whistles. Playable: players can teach dolphin pods human-like whistle patterns to coordinate group dives, or use human vocal mimicry to calm stressed pods.

Acoustic masking vs echolocation. Human vessel noise and seismic pulses scatter dolphin prey and mask signature whistles; dolphins counter by shifting click frequencies and using bubble curtains to break acoustic shadows. Playable: players can deploy low-frequency hums to disrupt dolphin sonar, or switch to silent hand signals to restore coordination.

Fire exploitation. Ravens drop smoldering twigs into dry grass to flush prey, mimicking human controlled burns. Humans counter with smoke screens and firebreaks to drive ravens from caches. Playable: players can use raven fire-flushing to reveal hidden resources, but must manage smoke drift to avoid alerting rival factions.

Historical hunting pressure. Humans tracked pronghorn across Pleistocene-Holocene steppe corridors, using endurance and fire to exhaust them; pronghorn rely on speed and terrain to escape. Playable: players can use human pursuit tactics to corner pronghorn, or preserve migration routes to unlock stamina bonuses.

Vocal and tool transfer. Humans demonstrate fire-starting and cache-hiding; ravens observe, imitate, and improve the techniques, teaching players how to outsmart spatial traps. Playable: players can learn raven cache-retrieval patterns to find hidden resources, or use human teaching to train raven allies for distraction.
